1) Auth: we're currently debating between using long-lived API keys (rotate quarterly) vs building an OAuth/JWT flow (IdP -> short-lived token). Our security team prefers short-lived creds but wants a low-friction path for our devs. Do you recommend Redwood-issued service account JWTs, or a lightweight OAuth bridge?

2) Routing & multi-region: we want automatic routing to us-west for latency-sensitive requests but fall back to us-east in outages. What's the recommended header strategy?

3) Embeddings / reranker: we plan to call embeddings separately and run a local reranker. Any guidance on scoping keys and rate limits?

Would love a short written playbook we can hand to our platform team. Also can we lock a 30-min technical sync next week (prefer early morning PST)?

Sam — great questions, thanks for summarizing. Recap + recommended path below (keeping this intentionally pragmatic for a POC):

Recap of ask:
- Low-friction auth for devs + short-lived production creds for security
- Region-aware routing for latency with graceful fallback
- Separate keys/scopes for embeddings vs generation/rerank calls
\Recommendation (POC-friendly):
1) Lightweight OAuth bridge + short-lived JWT service tokens (recommended)
   - Pattern: SignalPath IdP mint -> exchange for Redwood short-lived JWT (1h) bound to a service account
   - Why: minimal engineering on your side (use existing IdP), tokens expire quickly, Redwood enforces key-scoped permissions and audit logging
   - Fallback: Managed API keys scoped to environment if you need an emergency opt-in for legacy systems
\2) Rotation & key ops
   - Rotation cadence: 1 hour short-lived JWTs; root/longer-lived service account keys rotated 90 days and stored in customer KMS for Private deployments
   - Revoke path: immediate revocation via API for compromised service accounts
\3) Routing headers
   - Use x-redwood-region: us-west-1 preferred for primary; automatic geo-failover configured in the routing policy (we can pre-wire this in Dedicated/Private)
\4) Embeddings / reranker
   - Separate credential for embeddings with lower rate limits and dedicated quota to avoid noisy generation traffic affecting embeddings throughput
   - Recommend tagging embedding requests with x-redwood-purpose: embedding to help observability and cost attribution
\Attachments: I attached a lightweight checklist and a sample JWT exchange config to help your infra team.

Next steps
- Marissa (cc) will scope a 2-week mini-POC (staging access, sample prompts, basic metrics)
- Can you confirm which IdP you're using and whether you have a staging cluster for SignalPath?
- Proposed technical sync: Tue 2027-06-22 08:30 PST (tell us if that works)

Subject: Re: Post-demo: Redwood integration recap — SE notes + examples

Sam — adding a few concrete SE notes to make the POC setup frictionless. I'm pasting short examples you can use in staging: 

Token exchange (example)
1) Client authenticates with IdP and receives id_token
2) POST /v1/token/exchange to Redwood with id_token -> response {"access_token": "ey...", "expires_in": 3600}

cURL (exchange)
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/token/exchange \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{"id_token":"<id_token>","aud":"signalpath-poc"}'

Call using short-lived JWT
curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer <access_token>\" -H \"x-redwood-region: us-west-1\" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate

Embedding separation
- Issue a separate credential scoped to embeddings.read and embeddings.create; apply lower QPS but larger batch-size to optimize cost.
\Reranker guidance
- Local reranker should call /v1/embeddings to fetch vector IDs and then run similarity locally. Keep the reranker key scoped read-only to vectors to limit blast radius.
\POC checklist (what we need from you)
- Staging URL + test dataset (50 doc sample)
- IdP metadata (issuer, JWKS URL) or service account to test exchange flow
- List of endpoints you plan to call (generation vs embeddings vs eval)
\I'll create a short repo with the curl examples and a minimal Node SDK snippet before our sync.
\--Marissa Cole

Looping in security notes — quick checklist from compliance/ops: 
- For POC: short-lived JWTs (1h) are fine; require token binding to client_id and IP-range where possible.
- For production Private deployment: we recommend customer-managed KMS and optional mutual TLS for control plane calls.
- Audit: enable token exchange logging and push logs to your SIEM via our delivery endpoint.
- Evidence: we'll share the SOC 2 summary and our key rotation policy (I will attach in follow-up).
\Rishi
